newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bukaka says to meet 1996 net target.
newsitem.headline: Bukaka says to meet 1996 net target.

text.p: Indonesian transport, energy and engineering firm PT Bukaka Teknik Utama said on Tuesday that it was confident it would achieve its net profit target of 46 billion rupiah for 1996.
Bukaka's president director Fadel Muhammad said although first-half results were substantially below half the full-year forecast, the company would meet its target.
He said in a statement the Eid al-Fitr holiday period in February and late government approval of some projects prevented the company from reaching its full potential in the first half.
The company posted net profit of 14.3 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1996 against 6.1 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
The firm also said in the statement that it secured new projects worth 141 billion rupiah in July and August.

The energy division obtained three projects totalling 88 billion rupiah, the plant system division won tender bids worth 35 billion rupiah while the telecommunications division was awarded an 11 billion rupiah construction contract.
The transportation and aero-space division recorded new contracts worth seven billion rupiah at airports in Indonesia and Japan, the statement said.
"With the addition of these new projects to our current contracts on hand, I am confident that we have more than enough projects for 1997," Muhammad said.
